text:
anya: Quick check — CI started failing on the new async streaming tests after the poetry lock update. Error is a typing mismatch from httpcore/httpx stubs. Anyone else hit this?
kevin: Yep, saw that on my branch. stack trace points to `httpcore._sync.connection.Response` vs the async variant, looks like httpcore/HTTPX got mixed versions between deps.
sam: Did we pin httpcore anywhere in pyproject? I only see `httpx = "^0.24"` and no explicit httpcore, so poetry might have pulled 0.17 vs 0.16 depending on resolver timing.
olivia: I think this is the lock-race we discussed — CI runs `poetry lock` on older runner images then tests run with `pip install -r requirements.txt` exported from the lock, sometimes leading to mismatch when local dev adds an indirect.
anya: Repro steps that worked for me: `git checkout fix/async-streaming`, then `poetry lock --no-update`, `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes > reqs.txt`, `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r reqs.txt`, run tests -> passes. If I do `poetry install` first then export, tests fail.
kevin: ugh. So ordering matters. For a quick workaround we can pin `httpcore = "0.17.0"` in pyproject extras for now. But that's ugly.
sam: Alternative: add a CI step that runs `poetry lock` inside the same runner image and then export, to avoid different resolvers. Also we should add a tiny integration test that asserts consistent httpx/httpcore pair.
olivia: For the typing error specifically, adding `typing-extensions` pinned to the same version helped in one env. But that felt like a bandaid.
ci-bot: :information_source: New pipeline job started: devex/py-typing-checks (triggered by anya).
anya: I'm leaning toward pin + CI fix. I'll open a tiny PR that pins httpcore in pyproject and adds the CI `poetry lock` step. Can someone review? cc @kevin @sam
kevin: I can review after standup. Also leave a note in changelog with rationale.
sam: If you want a less invasive change, we could add a constraints.txt produced by `pip-compile` and use `pip install -c constraints.txt -r reqs.txt`. That way pip-invoked installs still respect the resolved set.
olivia: That is robust, but adds tooling (pip-tools) to the pipeline. Worth it if we keep hitting this.
anya: Drafting PR now. Patch snippet I'm trying:
```toml
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.11"
httpx = "^0.24"
httpcore = "0.17.0"  # pin to avoid async/sync mixups in CI
```
kevin: Small note — add a comment about why pinned and link this thread. Also mention any targeted CVE/compat reason in case ops asks.
anya: Will do. Also adding a short test in tests/integration/test_streaming.py that runs this minimal async generator:
```py
async def test_streaming_client_basic():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        async with client.stream('GET', 'http://localhost:8000/stream') as r:
            async for chunk in r.aiter_bytes():
                assert isinstance(chunk, (bytes, bytearray))
                break
```
kevin: Nice. Keep it tiny so CI doesn't flake.
sam: I'll update the CI job tomorrow to run `poetry lock` before export and add a short blurb in the README dev setup to avoid local confusion.
olivia: Assigning review to @kevin. If he doesn't get to it by EOD, I'll do a quick pass.
anya: Thanks all — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/482 (WIP). I'll mark as ready for review when CI green.
ci-bot: :white_check_mark: Pipeline devex/py-typing-checks passed for commit 6a7b2c.
